clips.title: The story
paras: Pilot Hammerfoot fears the worst for his comrade, Mori Hildelve, who ventured into the craggy hills of Dun Morogh on foot after wrecking his siege engine. Hildelve was searching for a rare ore vital for potent blastpowder, but days have passed amidst unsettling roars echoing through the peaks.

Dwarven siege engines are formidable war machines, but even iron treads struggle against the treacherous, jagged ridges of Dun Morogh. While scouring the slopes for a rare mineral deposit required to produce high-grade blastpowder, Pilot Mori Hildelve pushed his engine too far up a steep hill and busted the machine. Undeterred by the breakdown, Hildelve ordered his companion, Pilot Hammerfoot, to stay behind and guard the broken machinery while he pressed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot.

Days went by with no sign of Hildelve returning to camp. In the dead of night, strange and vicious beastly growls began echoing down from the rocky crags, turning Hammerfoot's mild impatience into creeping dread. Though Hildelve had a reputation for being as tough as nails, surviving the frigid heights of Dun Morogh without mechanized armor or heavy support against prowling predators is a dangerous gamble.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: My friend and fellow Siege Engine pilot, Mori Hildelve, is lost in the hills. We were looking for a rare ore that's needed for a high-grade blastpowder, and during our search he drove his engine up a steep hill and busted it!
Still convinced that ore was in these mountains, Hildelve charged me to guard our engines while he continued on foot, searching.
It's been days, and I've heard some beastly growls in the hills at night. Mori's tough as nails, but I'm worried.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Here is the corpse of a dwarf -- mauled, frozen, and picked clean by mountain scavengers. Clutched in its hand is a book containing the roughly scribbled notes of Mori Hildelve. And around its frame, still in superior condition, is a Brigadier's Vest.
This grisly scene must have been where the Siege Engine pilot met his end.
